channel.title: Congress Report Card weekly digest
channel.description: Missed votes, grade changes and bills that became law, every Saturday.

item.title: Week ending November 21, 2026
item.description:
Here is what changed in the public record of Congress from November 14 to November 21, 2026.

Votes this week

The House held 4 roll-call votes and the Senate held 17 roll-call votes. 450 of the 533 members who could vote cast every vote.

Most votes missed this week

  1. Christopher Murphy (D, CT) missed 17 of 17
  2. Amy Klobuchar (D, MN) missed 11 of 17
  3. Bill Cassidy (R, LA) missed 10 of 17
  4. John Cornyn (R, TX) missed 10 of 17
  5. Tommy Tuberville (R, AL) missed 10 of 17
  6. Cory A. Booker (D, NJ) missed 8 of 17
  7. Katie Boyd Britt (R, AL) missed 8 of 17
  8. Christopher A. Coons (D, DE) missed 8 of 17
  9. Richard J. Durbin (D, IL) missed 6 of 17
  10. Mitch McConnell (R, KY) missed 6 of 17

Bills that became law

  • HR 10167: Common Cents Act. Sponsored by Lisa C. McClain (R, MI-9).

Grade changes

43 members moved to a different letter grade. Bill scores are ranked within each chamber, so a grade can move when other members' records change.

Biggest gains

  • Mark Kelly (D, AZ): C to C+
  • Elizabeth Warren (D, MA): B- to B
  • Jefferson Shreve (R, IN-6): C+ to B-
  • Judy Chu (D, CA-28): A- to A
  • Emily Randall (D, WA-6): C to C+

Biggest drops

  • Christopher Murphy (D, CT): C- to D
  • John Cornyn (R, TX): B+ to B
  • Bill Cassidy (R, LA): C+ to C
  • Tommy Tuberville (R, AL): D to D-
  • Katie Boyd Britt (R, AL): C+ to C

See every member's grade at congressreportcard.org, or read how grades are calculated.
